## Highlights

Steno 0.13 makes themes more composable, separates the reusable build and template layers into
their own packages, and adds stronger release checks around the packages people actually install.

## Themes and templates

- Themes can now be loaded from directories and extend another theme, making shared foundations
  practical without duplicating layouts and assets ([#215](https://github.com/stenopress/steno/pull/215)).
- Themes can compose multiple layouts, define scoped template functions and filters, and use named
  slots in Tau components ([#255](https://github.com/stenopress/steno/pull/255), [#258](https://github.com/stenopress/steno/pull/258), [#259](https://github.com/stenopress/steno/pull/259)).
- Theme configuration schemas now support `oneOf` and `anyOf`
  ([#256](https://github.com/stenopress/steno/pull/256)).
- Added `slugify`, `pluralize`, `number`, and inline Markdown template filters
  ([#257](https://github.com/stenopress/steno/pull/257)).
- Sites can include a custom CSS file from `public/`, and Steno now includes CSS and HTML
  minification support ([#213](https://github.com/stenopress/steno/pull/213), [#223](https://github.com/stenopress/steno/pull/223)).

## Development and scaffolding

- Trusted local plugins now hot-reload during `steno dev`
  ([#260](https://github.com/stenopress/steno/pull/260)).
- File watching now resolves symlinks when comparing changes, avoiding missed rebuilds in linked
  projects ([#217](https://github.com/stenopress/steno/pull/217)).
- The development server now handles failed build hooks and browser live-reload cleanup more
  reliably ([#219](https://github.com/stenopress/steno/pull/219), [#221](https://github.com/stenopress/steno/pull/221)).
- `@steno/init` now emits the current top-level configuration shape, including theme, theme config,
  and short-URL settings ([#291](https://github.com/stenopress/steno/pull/291)).

## Packages and API stability

- Steno’s content pipeline is now published as `@steno/core`, while Tau is published as
  `@steno/tau`. `@steno/steno` remains the build orchestrator, and compatibility exports remain
  available ([#263](https://github.com/stenopress/steno/pull/263)).
- Public package exports are now checked as explicit contracts, helping prevent accidental API drift
  across future releases ([#288](https://github.com/stenopress/steno/pull/288)).

## Release confidence

- Added clean-registry consumer tests that exercise the packages as users install them, including
  official themes and isolated plugins ([#292](https://github.com/stenopress/steno/pull/292)).
- Release candidates now run representative sites and generated-project smoke tests on Linux,
  macOS, and Windows ([#294](https://github.com/stenopress/steno/pull/294)).
- Benchmark trends, module boundaries, and module-size budgets are checked in CI
  ([#249](https://github.com/stenopress/steno/pull/249), [#250](https://github.com/stenopress/steno/pull/250), [#252](https://github.com/stenopress/steno/pull/252), [#253](https://github.com/stenopress/steno/pull/253)).

## Dependencies

- Updated `marked` to 18.0.11 ([#237](https://github.com/stenopress/steno/pull/237), [#240](https://github.com/stenopress/steno/pull/240)).
